title: Continual-GraphLLM: Dynamic Graph Large Language Model with Invariance Regularized Adaptive Multi-Scale Experts

problem.claim: Continual learning on dynamic text-attributed graphs must adapt to evolving structural-textual patterns while retaining past knowledge.

gap.claim: Existing dynamic graph language-model methods struggle with jointly evolving graph structure and textual patterns.

contributions.claim: A continual-learning dynamic graph language-model framework routes incoming patterns to experts for similar past patterns and assigns new experts to unseen patterns.
A graph-text factor-based router adaptively activates suitable experts using latent factors.
Invariance-regularized multi-scale experts capture invariances among assigned patterns and progressively integrate structural and textual information from local to global scale.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe Continual-GraphLLM as a novel continual-learning dynamic graph language-model framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world dynamic text-attributed graphs reportedly show superiority over competitive baselines.
The authors report effectiveness in adapting to emerging dynamic text-attributed graph patterns.

narrative_sequence.summary: Dynamic text-attributed graphs combine textual and structural dynamics, motivating dynamic graph language models.
Continuously emerging nodes, edges, text, and interactions create evolving patterns that challenge existing methods and motivate continual learning.
Continual-GraphLLM routes incoming patterns to specialized experts and introduces experts for unseen patterns.
A graph-text factor router selects experts, while invariance-regularized multi-scale experts address forgetting across structural and textual scales.
The authors report favorable results on real-world dynamic text-attributed graphs against competitive baselines.

source_observation.claim: Jointly evolving structure and text require adaptation of structure, text, and graph-text fusion together.

interpretation.claim: Continual systems for multimodal relational data may need coordinated adaptation across modalities and their fusion mechanism.

application.claim: Use separate but coordinated adaptation mechanisms for relational structure, content, and cross-modal fusion in evolving graph systems.

exception.claim: This lesson may not apply when only one modality evolves or when cross-modal fusion is not central to the task.

source_observation.claim: Updating a model for new patterns can overwrite prior global graph-text fusion capabilities and bias it toward recent local dynamics.

interpretation.claim: Continual adaptation should explicitly protect stable knowledge while incorporating new local patterns.

application.claim: Consider expert routing, new-expert allocation, and invariance regularization when adapting models under pattern drift.

exception.claim: These mechanisms may be unnecessary when forgetting is acceptable or when the deployment objective prioritizes only recent patterns.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baseline identities, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the latent factors, expert architecture, training procedure, or computational costs.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
